reports.question: Which parts of a countable-group action's random structure are detected by generators, weak containment and finite models, and when do sofic approximation dependence, weak Pinsker obstructions and random-model entropy separate these notions?

reports.coverage_status: 45 atomic knowledge pages: 3001-300Z and 3010-3019 (base36 order), narrative outline 3000, reference icm2026-austin. All main report branches are represented: classical-to-group coding, generators/Rokhlin entropy, weak containment, finite approximations and sofic entropy, weak Pinsker and LDPC obstruction, random free-group models, zero-order/annealed/quenched entropy and open questions, representation analogy and AP entropy. Secondary constructions and deep proofs remain external as itemized below.

proof_scope.3001: Defines standard probability-preserving countable-group actions, ergodicity and almost-sure freeness; proves the common-conull-set observation and the nonatomic consequence for free ergodic infinite-group actions.
proof_scope.3002: Defines factor, isomorphism and independent direct-product factor; proves that a factor of an ergodic action is ergodic.
proof_scope.3003: Computes orbit-code equivariance and the coordinate inversion relating the existing shift convention. Generator/isomorphism equivalence uses the standard measurable inverse theorem as an explicit external input.
proof_scope.3004: Complete finite-base proof of almost-sure freeness for every countably infinite group, using infinitely many disjoint pairs and a probability strictly below one. Finite groups are explicitly excluded.
proof_scope.3005: Defines the left Folner condition, proves the integer interval example and finite-set union bound. Equivalence with invariant-mean amenability is cited.
proof_scope.3006: Defines Rokhlin entropy for ergodic actions using countable generating partitions. Records the invariant-sigma-algebra correction needed outside ergodicity. Amenable equality is cited only for free ergodic actions of countably infinite amenable groups.
proof_scope.3007: Seward's prescribed-distribution finite generator theorem is cited with nonatomic, ergodic, countably infinite group and strict entropy inequality assumptions; freeness is not imposed on this theorem. The classical equality case is explained by the Shannon independence equality criterion, not by a new proof of Seward.
proof_scope.3008: Cites Seward's Sinai theorem for free ergodic actions of countably infinite groups, including the non-strict base entropy bound. The nonamenable positive-entropy consequence uses the cited factor relation among Bernoulli shifts. Direct-product splitting is kept distinct.
proof_scope.3009: Complete calculation of the F2 Ornstein-Weiss edge-difference factor, including equivariance and finite-forest fiber counting giving independent output bits.
proof_scope.3010: Cites Bowen's Bethe-Kikuchi formula and the resulting limsup/liminf equality after neighborhood infimum. Proves product additivity directly from finite-block Shannon additivity and the formula.
proof_scope.3011: Complete elementary bounds between zero-order and annealed entropy from probability <= expected count <= alphabet-size exponential times probability. The rare-large-count example is explicitly an abstract integer-variable example, not a constructed dynamical system.
proof_scope.3012: Defines quenched entropy using expected log-plus model count on the zero-order-zero branch and -infinity otherwise, with log-plus(0)=0. Question 3.22 remains open at the report's scope.
proof_scope.3013: Cites the weak Pinsker three-entropy identity in the finite weak-Pinsker-entropy setting; interprets its two terms without interchanging expectation and logarithm.
proof_scope.3014: States Question 3.21 for general product actions and derives only the factor-monotonicity upper bound. Joint model events are not assumed independent.
proof_scope.3015: Proves positive definiteness by the Gram identity under the existing second-variable-linear convention and checks the Koopman group law/unitarity. GNS existence is cited.
proof_scope.3016: Defines scalar AP entropy with normalized Euclidean unit-ball volume and complex dimension in the exponent. Proves the scaling law by a real-volume Jacobian. General determinant and change-of-GNS-vector theorems are not reconstructed.
proof_scope.3017: Cites the mollification recovery formula for independent Haar unitary generator models, with normalized volumes as in 3016. The superexponential trace hypothesis and Lemma 7.3 were directly checked; determinant and three-entropy proofs remain external inputs.
proof_scope.3018: Complete periodic-measure density proof for every stationary finite-alphabet process, using independently sampled long blocks, variance estimates and cyclic boundary control. No ergodicity assumption or unproved ergodic decomposition step is needed.
proof_scope.3019: Cites Hayes's completely-positive-sofic-entropy Koopman embedding theorem in the form stated in report Theorem 3.7(e). Defines the embedding and left regular action explicitly; it is not a Bernoulli classification criterion.
proof_scope.300A: Defines weak containment by finite pattern distributions; proves equivalence to closure of observable laws, factor implication and transitivity.
proof_scope.300B: Abért-Weiss minimality is cited. Derives weak equivalence of nontrivial finite-base Bernoulli shifts, and distinguishes it from isomorphism using existing classical entropy calculations.
proof_scope.300C: Kakutani-Rokhlin tower lemma is cited in the nonatomic ergodic setting. Complete finite-window coloring argument proves weak simulation of a uniform finite cycle, with explicit error bound.
proof_scope.300D: Complete construction of a permutation approximation from a separating sequence of finite quotients; proves the converse and growth of quotient sizes for an infinite group. Reuses the existing fixed-point criterion.
proof_scope.300E: Defines sofic approximation by almost multiplicativity and asymptotic freeness; proves finite-window injectivity outside a vanishing bad set. Nonsofic existence is left an open problem at the report's scope.
proof_scope.300F: Complete partial-translation completion proof that a countably infinite amenable group is sofic, including multiplicative error and size growth.
proof_scope.300G: Defines root-weighted empirical distributions and model spaces. Verifies exact invariance for homomorphisms and explains the asymptotically invariant, not exactly invariant, sofic case.
proof_scope.300H: Complete diagonal proof that subsequential model realizability is equivalent to infinitely many models in each neighborhood. No all-large-size existence is inferred.
proof_scope.300I: Complete finite-window coding and measurable-approximation argument for passage of realizability along weak containment in the exact permutation-approximation setting. It is not presented as a model-count monotonicity theorem or as a full approximate-homomorphism proof.
proof_scope.300J: Defines finite-alphabet sofic entropy, proves its -infinity versus nonnegative alternatives and logarithmic alphabet bound. Isomorphism invariance and Kerr-Li's extension beyond finite generators are cited.
proof_scope.300K: Complete finite-base Bernoulli model-count calculation: good-root injectivity, independent-label variance bound, typical probability lower bound and multinomial/type upper bound. Zero-probability letters are handled by support restriction for the lower bound.
proof_scope.300L: Necessity of equal finite-base entropy follows from the proved Bernoulli formula and cited invariance; sufficiency uses Bowen-Seward's theorem. Countably infinite group is an explicit condition, not extended to finite groups.
proof_scope.300M: General sofic <= Rokhlin comparison is cited; the finite-generator counting bound is proved. Gives the two-cycle counterexample to blanket amenable Rokhlin=KS equality, and states the infinite-group free-ergodic zero-Rokhlin question precisely.
proof_scope.300N: Complete finite-alphabet product-subadditivity argument, including the -infinity case; additivity when one factor is Bernoulli is cited. No undefined infinity subtraction is used.
proof_scope.300O: Defines weak Pinsker splitting using arbitrarily small residual Rokhlin entropy and defines the supremal Bernoulli direct-factor entropy. Distinguishes the sofic variant and ordinary factor maps.
proof_scope.300P: Cites the weak Pinsker theorem restricted to free ergodic actions of countably infinite amenable groups. No assertion of a single exactly zero-entropy residual factor is made.
proof_scope.300Q: Cites the general approximation-independence lemma for weak Pinsker systems. Expands the elementary squeezing argument only when the chosen Bernoulli bases are finite and residual systems have finite generators; general standard-base and infinite-entropy cases remain cited.
proof_scope.300R: Defines the compact binary parity-check shift for the free product of r cyclic groups with k>r>=3, proves closed subgroup and shift invariance, and obtains the Haar-preserving action from existing Haar theory.
proof_scope.300S: Cites the LDPC construction's ergodicity, no nontrivial Bernoulli direct factor and non-weak-containment in Bernoulli. Specifies the independent k-uniform permutation law and prechosen high-probability sets: every selection has the stated entropy along every subsequence and completely positive entropy along the selected approximation. Derives failure of weak Pinsker from the cited structure and sofic-Rokhlin inequality.
proof_scope.300T: Complete fixed-word collision estimate for independent uniform generator permutations, giving expected fixed points O(1) and freeness in probability. Almost-sure approximation is asserted only after a summable-error subsequence choice.
proof_scope.300U: Defines zero-order entropy for finite-alphabet processes and extends it by the infimum over all finite observables. Records range [-infinity,0] and separates existence probability from model number.
proof_scope.300V: Proves the weak-containment inequality for zero-order entropy using uniform finite-window model transfer and event inclusion; extends to the observable definition.
proof_scope.300W: States Questions 3.15(a,b) as questions. Proves the elementary diagonal subexponential-probability subsequence observation; the concentration upgrade to subsequential high probability is cited, not treated as an elementary implication of zero exponential rate.
proof_scope.300X: States Question 3.17 with the infimum over neighborhoods outside limsup/liminf. Does not replace it by a claim of convergence for every fixed neighborhood.
proof_scope.300Y: Complete finite-graph identity between a balanced cut's normalized edge count and root statistics, retaining generator edge multiplicities. The convergence statement is cited only conditional on Question 3.15(a).
proof_scope.300Z: Defines annealed sofic entropy with expectation before logarithm, finite-generator scope and possible finite negative values. Isomorphism invariance is cited.

remaining_branches: Deep proofs remain cited: Ornstein/Bowen-Seward classification, prescribed generators and Sinai factors, Abért-Weiss, entropy invariance and Kerr-Li extension, weak Pinsker, LDPC clustering/CPE, Hayes spectral embedding, Bowen Bethe-Kikuchi formula, AP determinant and three-entropy machinery.

Gaussian functor and Connes-Feldman-Weiss/orbit-equivalence proof machinery mentioned by the report are not given new atomic constructions; these are secondary supporting branches, not claimed reconstructed.

General nonergodic conditional Rokhlin entropy, full standard-base/infinite-entropy extensions, and the full sofic approximate-homomorphism version of the finite-window transfer proof are not expanded. Local proof scopes are stated page by page.

LDPC stronger inherited entropy and quantitative approximate-direct-factorization bound are not separately developed. Ordinary completely positive entropy and no exact nontrivial Bernoulli direct factor are the integrated consequences.
Planted random models, surface-group random permutation models and general matrix-valued AP/CP-map theory remain unexpanded secondary directions.

Questions 3.1, 3.10, 3.15(a,b), 3.17, 3.21 and 3.22 remain questions at the report's scope; Corollary 3.16 remains conditional. Existence of nonsofic groups is not inferred from the Aldous-Lyons developments.
normalization_notes: Left shift S^g(z)_h=z_(g^-1 h) and orbit code alpha(T^(h^-1)x). Existing 00SA has the conjugate right-index convention; coordinate inversion J is calculated in 3003 rather than changing the existing page.

All logarithms are natural. Bernoulli entropy formula and classification are restricted to countably infinite groups where required. Nontrivial finite-group Bernoulli actions need not be almost surely free.

Rokhlin entropy uses countable generating partitions. Finite generators are conclusions requiring strict bounds, not tacit assumptions on every action. Nonergodic definitions require conditioning on the invariant sigma algebra.

Rokhlin=KS amenable comparison is restricted to free ergodic actions of countably infinite amenable groups. The finite periodic two-cycle example demonstrates why an unrestricted blanket equality is false.

Empirical distributions average over roots with multiplicity. For general sofic approximations neighborhoods lie in all probability measures; empirical distributions need not themselves be exactly invariant.
Finite-alphabet deterministic sofic entropy is -infinity or nonnegative. Nonnegative entropy only ensures arbitrarily late models in every shrinking neighborhood, not all-large-n realizability.
Annealed entropy uses log E(model count), not E log(model count), and may be finite negative. Quenched entropy uses log-plus with value zero at zero and an explicit zero-order branch condition.

The LDPC approximation law is independent uniform k-cycle-only permutations for k dividing n; the prechosen high-probability sets quantify uniformly over subsequent choices. It is not a theorem for arbitrary sofic approximations.
The entropy limit questions compare inf_O limsup and inf_O liminf, not convergence for each fixed neighborhood.

AP volume normalization makes the complex d-dimensional unit ball have volume one; the speed is d, not real dimension 2d. The inner product is linear in the second variable, so the type is <v,pi(g)v>.
Terminology is 殆周期熵 (almost periodic entropy, AP entropy), as requested in parent review. No externally verified Banana Space terminology entry is claimed.
Existing 可和 terminology is retained for amenability; sofic, Rokhlin, Bernoulli, annealed/退火 and quenched/淬火 remain consistent with the local note vocabulary.

reports.question: How do robust tangencies obstruct finite statistical descriptions, how do renormalizations implant arbitrary local models, and how does emergence distinguish complexity of orbit statistics from periodic-point growth or metric entropy? Which conclusions are residual, positive-measure, generic-family almost-every-parameter or every-parameter, and in which dimension, map class and regularity?
reports.reading_scope: Complete official mathematical report sections 1.1-3.4, all numbered results/questions, footnotes and bibliography read, rather than abstract only; relevant official PDF text cross-checked. Figures were not visually inspected. Supplementary primary sources were read only in the explicitly listed scopes below. Original Newhouse, GST, Kaloshin, Berger-Biebler, SRB, KAM, Oseledets and Pesin proofs are external inputs, not claimed reconstructed.
reports.coverage_status: 46 independent knowledge pages, one narrative outline and one reference. Wild hyperbolicity and finite-regularity parameter quantifiers, primitive renormalization and universality, entropy prerequisites, statistical emergence and analytic pseudo-rotation branches are covered with separate local hypotheses. Strong regularity and standard-map motivation are bounded narrative context, not new claimed theorems. No full research-theorem proof or whole-repository validation is claimed.

proof_scope.3101: Defines local versus global diffeomorphisms and joint finite/smooth family topology; gives a covering-map example separating local invertibility from global injectivity.
proof_scope.3102: Defines uniform hyperbolic splitting on a compact invariant set; no structural stability or stable-manifold theorem is folded into this definition.
proof_scope.3103: Defines saddle stable/unstable sets and quadratic homoclinic tangency; elementary normal separation calculation. Existence of leaves is delegated to 311A.
proof_scope.3104: Complete adapted-norm contraction proof, using Jordan decomposition and nilpotence; proves the entire basin is a nonempty open union of inverse images and computes periodic empirical averages.
proof_scope.3105: Defines robust tangency of varying leaves of a continued basic set. No claim that a fixed tangency point persists.
proof_scope.3106: Newhouse's sink-creation theorem is external; the countable open-dense intersection producing infinitely many sinks is proved.
proof_scope.3107: Complete construction of a residual null set by small open neighborhoods of rational points.
proof_scope.3108: Defines generic-family/almost-every-parameter quantifiers and distinguishes the stronger every-parameter conclusion and the zero-dimensional case.
proof_scope.3109: Cites finite-regularity all-parameter infinite-sink theorem with annulus local-diffeomorphism versus dimension-at-least-three diffeomorphism distinction. Parablender mechanism is explicitly an outline, not a full proof; C-infinity extension remains conjectural.
proof_scope.3110: Defines maximal oscillation; proves two distinct invariant cluster measures force failure of a continuous observable's time average. Quadratic/rational maximal-order existence theorems and quantitative lower bounds remain external.
proof_scope.3111: Complete proof that asymptotic stability is open, that a stable component consists of one asymptotic class, and that asymptotic orbits have identical empirical cluster sets by a Cesaro W1 bound.
proof_scope.3112: Cites degree-six real Henon wandering domains and Cr/analytic Newhouse-domain density. Positive-order and complex Fatou conclusions are external; no residual or full-measure upgrade.
proof_scope.3113: Defines corrected double-log pointwise and averaged local-order conventions; checks elementary mass examples. Helfter's pointwise comparison is external, and only its integration consequence is derived. No exchange of integral and limsup.
proof_scope.3114: Cites analytic pseudo-rotations of maximal averaged local order on annulus, sphere and disk, reusing 0P analytic/AbC foundations. Does not identify this with an ergodic construction or prove the analytic approximation theorem anew.
proof_scope.3115: Defines physical measure and states only the fixed-small-nonzero-b Henon-family consequence of the report's broader robustness theorem. Parameter exclusion and SRB/basin conclusions are external.
proof_scope.3119: Separates basic-set/local-maximality definitions from the cited hyperbolic continuation theorem; period preservation uses existing conjugacy theory.
proof_scope.310A: Defines the report's robust projection property of unstable leaves of a continued hyperbolic basic set. No unproved claim about full-dimensional interior of the set itself.
proof_scope.310B: Complete Taylor remainder, Leibniz and rescaled-cutoff estimate for a vanishing jet. Does not turn a finite differentiability estimate into a uniform analytic or C-infinity parameter construction.
proof_scope.310C: Explicit inverse, Jacobian determinant and area factor of generalized Henon maps; distinguishes b=0, b nonzero and b=1.
proof_scope.310D: Defines primitive renormalization, conformally symplectic charts and the disjoint N-level return tower.
proof_scope.310E: Complete proof that a q-periodic model orbit lifts to exact period Nq, using all tower levels, plus similarity of derivative return maps.
proof_scope.310F: Complete Baire argument extracting a common-period open subset from a periodic spot; analytic obstruction uses 311B.
proof_scope.310G: Cites multi-tangency polynomial Henon renormalization with independent unfolding, connected saddles, dissipative/symplectic distinction and finite-order error estimates. No full rescaling proof.
proof_scope.310H: Cites arbitrary periodic-point creation and proves the Baire conclusion. Counts hyperbolic fixed points of f^k, not necessarily points of exact period k.
proof_scope.310I: Cites the finite-r all-parameter arbitrary-growth result. Does not claim a common subsequence for all parameters or a C-infinity/analytic extension.
proof_scope.310J: Defines universality by density of primitive renormalizations, distinguishing orientation-preserving and symplectic model classes and approximation from equality.
proof_scope.310K: States the separate high-dimensional C1 and surface Cr universality theorems, with the higher-regularity high-dimensional branch left open.
proof_scope.310L: Cites the exact near-identity renormalization theorem for ball diffeomorphisms; the analogous exact symplectic statement remains a question.
proof_scope.310M: States precise simple elliptic spectrum, low-order nonresonance and invertible Birkhoff twist matrix from BT25b Definition 2.1. No proof of the normal form or KAM persistence.
proof_scope.310N: Defines localizable, openly localizable and generically localizable properties in the smooth symplectic setting.
proof_scope.310O: Cites BT25b Theorem E in the jointly C-infinity nondegenerate elliptic family space and proves only its countable-conjunction consequence.
proof_scope.310P: Deduces the all-parameter generic symplectic universality conclusion from the cited localizability proposition and Theorem E.
proof_scope.310Q: Cites Berger-Turaev positive-area-entropy perturbation near an elliptic point. Construction paragraph is a proof outline. Separates analytic/billiard/geodesic open problems.
proof_scope.310R: Complete telescoping proof that empirical-measure cluster points are invariant.
proof_scope.310S: Complete metric separation, Lipschitz approximation and finite-net proof that the dual W1 metric induces weak convergence on compact spaces.
proof_scope.310T: Deduces simultaneous convergence against all continuous functions from Birkhoff on a countable dense family and compactness; ergodic decomposition is a cited structural theorem.
proof_scope.310U: Defines statistical emergence and proves its conservative average-quantization formulation by dominated convergence; distinguishes positive order from merely superpolynomial growth.
proof_scope.310V: Complete finite-atomic quantization argument giving eventual exact emergence count; ergodic case gives one.
proof_scope.310W: Complete grid upper bound and arbitrary-center barycenter lower bound on the cube, proving polynomial emergence and zero order.
proof_scope.310X: Complete finite-space-net and mass-rounding upper bound proving emergence order at most manifold dimension.

proof_scope.310Z: Cites maximal-emergence local construction and derives all-parameter genericity from BT25b Proposition 1.6 and Theorem E, with exact dimension upper bound from 310X.
proof_scope.311A: States the stable-manifold theorem for every x in a compact hyperbolic set, not just periodic points. General theorem is external; the diagonal linear example is directly computed.
proof_scope.311B: Complete open-and-closed Taylor identity theorem on connected real-analytic manifolds. The hypothesis is equality on a nonempty open set, not equality outside an arbitrary open region.

remaining_branches.scope: Newhouse sink creation, parablenders, polynomial renormalization, universality constructions, KAM persistence and parameter-family localizability, positive-entropy implantation, wandering Fatou components and analytic realization are not reproduced as full proofs.

Oseledets and Pesin are cited with compactness, differentiability, invertibility and measure assumptions. Original proof PDFs were not read. The local norm-invariance, two-dimensional specialization and dominated-convergence calculations are explicit.

Main Conjecture 1.8 remains conjectural in the general C-infinity setting; Problems 1.10-1.11 on positive parameter measure and larger Hausdorff dimension are not inferred from residuality. Surface global diffeomorphisms are not substituted for annulus local diffeomorphisms.

Higher-dimensional Cr, r>=2, nonconservative universality; exact symplectic near-identity renormalization; analytic surface and conservative polynomial universality remain Questions/Problems 2.11-2.14.

Analytic disk perturbations, elliptic billiards and integrable surface geodesic flows retain Problems 2.16-2.18. Question 2.19 is not resolved. No analytic or arbitrary-parameter entropy theorem is inferred from a smooth single-map perturbation.

Maximal-order all-parameter genericity is stated only in the jointly C-infinity nondegenerate elliptic symplectic setting. Main Problem 3.5 and broader nonconservative typicality remain open. Maximal oscillation examples are self-maps, not diffeomorphisms.

3113 distinguishes integral of pointwise limsup from limsup of integrals. 3114 uses the averaged convention of the primary analytic papers. No unconditional equality between the conventions is asserted.

The report's return-box/folding architecture and positive-measure Henon consequence are explained. Full combinatorial strong-regularity criteria, Cantor inclusion estimates, Lorenz computer-assisted verification and standard-map numerical claims are not expanded.

No diagram was needed for the elementary arguments and no image-only source figures are reproduced. Parent owns global deduplication, registries, normalizeFormat, build, browser and publication checks.

normalization_notes: Definition 2.1 in both the official report and arXiv:2510.12929v1 prints disjoint tower levels 0<=k<n, where n is ambient dimension although N is return time. 310D uses 0<=k<N. This is an editorial mathematical correction supported by the return-tower definition, not a claim that the preprint already corrects it. The correction is recorded only here, not in public source metadata.

Official Theorem 2.7 combines Symp_e^infinity notation with C^r prose. 310P does not infer all finite-r or analytic versions: it uses BT25b v1 Theorems C/E and Proposition 1.5 on jointly C-infinity families in the nondegenerate elliptic open set. The stronger every-parameter quantifier is attributed to that primary theorem.
Periodic counts in 310H/310I are hyperbolic fixed points of f^k; exact periods may divide k. Exact Nq period is asserted only in 310E under the N-level disjoint-return hypothesis.

The official local-order display before Definition 3.11 has |log mass|/log|log epsilon| in both HTML and PDF text. 3113 instead uses the exponential-order double-log normalization verified in Helfter and the analytic primary papers. This source-display issue is not copied into mathematical bodies.

3113 uses log(1+|log mass|) to give atoms and mass-one balls the natural zero-order value. Positive-order small-mass asymptotics agree with the usual log|log mass| formula. It explicitly separates pointwise-integrated and averaged-before-limsup conventions.
Emergence order uses log log max{e,E(epsilon)} to define order zero for bounded emergence. This normalization does not alter any positive-order conclusion.

3102 now contains only the uniform hyperbolicity definition. Basic sets/continuation are isolated in 3119, and the stable-manifold theorem for every x in a hyperbolic set is isolated in 311A. 3103/3105/310A/310G link these prerequisites.

3104 proves basin equality B=union_{n>=0} f^{-n}(union_{0<=j<q} f^j(D)), hence the whole basin is open; it reuses 0F0D Jordan decomposition and 0F01 nilpotence. Its dependency on empirical-measure page 310R does not return to sinks.
310B records finite-order Taylor, chain-rule and Leibniz estimates and links the calculus prerequisites. It makes no analyticity or all-derivative cutoff assertion.
311B uses equality on one nonempty open set. The earlier phrase 'identity outside a nonempty open region' was removed because that outside set need not contain any open subset.
3112 explicitly identifies Henon complexification as an automorphism of C^2, two complex coordinates, not of C.

311C now states: if the measure is ergodic, the exponents and multiplicities are almost everywhere constant. Ergodicity is sufficient, not necessary; an identity map with a nonergodic measure already has constant zero exponents.

311D restricts the Pesin formula to a compact boundaryless C-infinity diffeomorphism preserving smooth positive area. The derivative-integral argument is separate from the external entropy theorem. No arbitrary invariant-measure or higher-dimensional maximum-only formula is asserted.

reports.title: Integrable Billiards and Related Topics
reports.outline_title: 可积台球：从反射守恒量到形状刚性
reports.version_role: Official published ICM2026 Volume 5 proceedings, online 2026-07-13. The official full HTML report, not an abstract or an arXiv substitute, is the primary source. Supplementary papers have separately fixed versions.

The reference page attributes the Chinese adaptation and independent calculations. Supplementary arXiv nonexclusive distribution licenses are not treated as translation or image-reuse permissions.
reports.question: How do variational reflection laws and invariant curves constrain the shape of a billiard table, and how do global, boundary-local, polynomial, and symmetry-assisted integrability differ across length, area, magnetic, Minkowski, wire, and cone models?
reports.reading_scope: Read the complete official mathematical text in sections 1-9, its displayed formulas and captions, bibliography and publication/license metadata. The image pixels were not visually inspected and no illustration-specific claim or image is reproduced. Supplementary full-text reading was selective and is recorded separately below; no supplementary research proof is represented as fully read when only its definitions, statements, or initial argument were consulted. Web content was treated as source data, not instructions.
reports.coverage_status: 51 atomic knowledge pages, 3201-321F in base36 order, one narrative outline 3200, and one reference. All major report branches have a mathematical entry point: classical reflection and integrability, four planar models, effective and symmetry-assisted rigidity, beta inequalities and equality, magnetic/Minkowski variants, wires, cones, and the corresponding open questions. Elementary local calculations are developed; deep rigidity, Aubry-Mather, and cone-classification proofs remain cited results.

proof_scope.3201: Derives the support-function parameterization, curvature radius, perimeter and translation terms for C2 positive-curvature convex curves; reuses the existing support-function definition.
proof_scope.3202: Derives the Euclidean reflection formula by tangential and normal decomposition, and explains the regular next collision for a strictly convex table.
proof_scope.3203: Computes the first variation of every finite fixed-endpoint broken-line length and derives the reflection equation at each vertex.
proof_scope.3204: Defines the exact symplectic positive twist convention p=-S_1, P=S_2, S_12<0 and checks preservation of the canonical two-form by differentiation.
proof_scope.3205: Computes the mixed derivative of chord length, the positive twist derivative, the invariant density sin(theta) ds dtheta, and its total mass 2P.
proof_scope.3206: Defines rotational invariant curves and the restricted circle map. Birkhoff's graph theorem is cited only for area-preserving positive twist maps isotopic to the identity; rotation-number existence is proved in 321D.
proof_scope.3207: Defines total integrability on a specified annular region and separates whole-phase-space, boundary-neighborhood, and table-perturbation meanings. No equivalence with an arbitrary single first integral is asserted.
proof_scope.3208: Computes the circle billiard map explicitly and checks its invariant constant-angle curves and total integrability.
proof_scope.3209: Defines a caustic through tangent trajectories and explains the circle example and smooth convex caustic/invariant-curve correspondence in its nondegenerate domain.
proof_scope.3210: Derives the Larmor circle radius and free-flight center for constant magnetic field and computes the center change under specular reflection.
proof_scope.3211: Cites magnetic total-integrability rigidity only in the weak-field range 0<B<kappa_min. Strong and variable-field extensions are retained as open questions.
proof_scope.3212: Defines the possibly asymmetric Minkowski gauge and derives the tangential momentum reflection equation by varying the norm-length action.
proof_scope.3213: Cites the finite-order symmetry enhancement and the global ellipse theorem with the k mod 4 distinction. Gives the elementary even-power lp symmetry obstruction; no invalid repeated enhancement is applied when k is 2 mod 4.
proof_scope.3214: Defines wire billiards by equal tangential projections of incoming and outgoing chords, retaining their possible multivalued nature. The closed nonplanar three-dimensional example problem remains open.
proof_scope.3215: Proves the linear-in-velocity conserved quantity <Ax,v> for a skew-symmetric orbit curve, both along free segments and at wire reflections; checks equality of the endpoint tangent-angle data.
proof_scope.3216: Proves closure, embeddedness, regularity and nonplanarity for the coprime two-frequency curve in R4, and computes its conserved quantity and constant-parameter-increment solutions. Does not assert that every wire relation is single-valued.
proof_scope.3217: Cites finite reflection for C3 cone sections with positive definite scalar second fundamental form, excluding apex and tangency singularities. Distinguishes per-orbit finiteness from a uniform bound and cites the C2 infinite-reflection counterexample.
proof_scope.3218: Proves conservation of squared angular momentum and the corresponding centered sphere caustic by direct free-flight and reflection calculations. Individual angular momentum components need not be conserved.
proof_scope.3219: Cites the cone orbit-separation theorem with its regularity and singular-set qualifications. The 2n-1 integrals on a 2n-2-dimensional line phase space are not asserted independent or Poisson commuting.
proof_scope.320A: Proves the ellipse's quadratic first integral during free motion and reflection; derives the confocal-line discriminant (F-lambda)/((a-lambda)(b-lambda)) and the elliptic-caustic range 0<F<b.
proof_scope.320B: Defines velocity-polynomial integrability with the free-flow equation, boundary reflection identity, and nonconstancy on the unit-energy level. Separates it from total phase-space integrability.
proof_scope.320C: Cites Glutsyuk Theorem 1.6 and Corollary 1.7 for a bounded connected planar domain with C2 connected boundary. The conclusion does not assume algebraicity of the boundary. The algebraic rigidity proof is external.
proof_scope.320D: States the boundary-neighborhood Birkhoff-Poritsky conjecture as open and distinguishes it from perturbative results for tables close to an ellipse and from polynomial rigidity.
proof_scope.320E: Defines m-configurations using actual finite fixed-endpoint local maxima, expands their second variation, and links the complete tridiagonal equivalence/closedness proof in 321E. Inclusion of rotational invariant curves in the m-set is a cited twist-map result.
proof_scope.320F: States the centrally symmetric C2 positive-curvature period-four strip theorem with the full strip down to zero rotation, not an arbitrary neighborhood. Both foliation and all-m-orbit versions are cited; the Hopf-type proof is external.
proof_scope.320G: Defines the oriented midpoint-tangency rule of outer-area billiards and distinguishes it from interior reflection.
proof_scope.320H: Computes the Jacobians in tangent coordinates and proves that outer-area billiards preserve Euclidean area.
proof_scope.320I: Proves preservation of concentric circles for a circular outer-area table and transfers the map by affine conjugacy to homothetic ellipses.
proof_scope.320J: Defines the positive phase domain of symplectic billiards and its nonlocal parallel-chord rule, including the diagonal and two-periodic limiting boundaries.
proof_scope.320K: Derives the symplectic reflection condition from the variation of half the sum of determinants, and checks the mixed derivative and invariant two-form with the correct factor 1/2.
proof_scope.320L: Computes the circle symplectic map (s,t) to (t,2t-s), proves its constant-angle foliation, and transfers it to ellipses by affine equivariance.
proof_scope.320M: Defines the outer-length tangent-segment generating function on the normal-angle interval (0,pi). The geometric circle rule, general twist property, and confocal ellipse construction are cited. General outer-length integrability rigidity remains open.
proof_scope.320N: States global outer-area total-integrability rigidity precisely and links the existing Blaschke-Santalo inequality used in its proof. The global rigidity argument is cited, not reconstructed from that inequality alone.
proof_scope.320O: Cites global symplectic rigidity and the centrally symmetric period-four strip theorem. The latter concerns either full side of the period-four curve, up to the diagonal or two-periodic boundary, not an arbitrary thin strip.
proof_scope.320P: Cites the effective non-m-orbit measure bound in terms of the L2 distance of h from span(1,cos,sin), with its constant and curvature factor. Proves the zero-distance circle characterization and the elementary harmonic perturbation calculation.
proof_scope.320Q: Cites the centrally symmetric effective ellipse bound with the specified period-four region, constant 25*pi^2/32, curvature power three, and the L2 distance of h^2 on [0,pi]. Checks scaling and uses the proved harmonic ellipse criterion 321B.
proof_scope.320R: Cites the middle-strip estimate 3*kappa_min*(P^2-4*pi*A)/16 and its hypotheses. Derives the circular equality consequence using the explicit planar isoperimetric proof 321F.
proof_scope.320S: States the four finite-symmetry rigidity theorems with their respective Euclidean or linear symmetry hypotheses. Proves the finite-order linear conjugacy calculation, keeping R_(2*pi*m/k), gcd(m,k)=1, and identifying its cyclic subgroup rather than an incorrectly fixed generator.
proof_scope.320T: Defines Birkhoff orthogonality and Radon norms. The outer-area period-four characterization is cited; the order-four symmetry consequence follows from 320S.
proof_scope.320U: Defines beta for the four C2 positive-curvature bounded strictly convex table models, with classical rotation interval (0,1) and the other positive branches (0,1/2). Existence and independence of minimizing average action are cited Aubry-Mather results. Inner signs are negative and outer signs positive.
proof_scope.320V: Cites strict convexity, irrational differentiability, and the rational periodic-invariant-curve criterion only for the explicitly specified four billiard models and their rotation intervals. Derives the finite-symmetry consequence and cites the full central/global reconstruction results separately.
proof_scope.320W: Calculates all four circular beta formulas geometrically. Proves the finite equal-angle extremum by the supporting-tangent inequality for convex/concave functions, so the calculation concerns global extrema, not just stationary configurations; uses cited beta continuity for irrational limits.
proof_scope.320X: States the three beta isoperimetric inequalities with same perimeter for length models and same area for symplectic billiards. Outer-area billiards are excluded. Supplies the equal-angle trial-action calculation, while the complete comparison theorem remains cited.
proof_scope.320Y: Cites interior rational rigidity and the irrational Gutkin exception for classical billiards. Treats rho=1/2 separately: proves beta=-diameter and equality iff constant width for classical billiards, and records the trivial symplectic endpoint and divergent outer endpoints.
proof_scope.320Z: Cites centrally symmetric elliptic beta spectral rigidity and the special two-value determination result. Computes the diameter value directly and retains determination by arbitrary two beta values as an open question.
proof_scope.321A: Derives the support-function generator S=-2h*sin(delta) with canonical momentum equal to negative signed line distance, verifies its first and mixed derivatives, and proves its periodic sum equals negative perimeter by telescoping.
proof_scope.321B: Proves that a positive support function whose square is a positive second-harmonic quadratic expression is the support function of a centered ellipse, using linked Schwarz inequality and real symmetric diagonalization.
proof_scope.321C: Derives global classical circle rigidity from the cited effective bound, invariant-curve inclusion in the m-set, and the zero-distance support-function criterion. The reverse direction is the explicit circle computation.
proof_scope.321D: Gives a complete rotation-number existence proof for orientation-preserving circle homeomorphisms using oscillation of displacement at most one, subadditivity/superadditivity, and the division n=qk+r argument. No unproved Fekete lemma is used.
proof_scope.321E: Proves equivalence of all finite local maxima, all finite negative semidefinite Hessians, and all finite negative definite Hessians for the positive-twist tridiagonal system, using zero extension into larger intervals. Proves closedness by passing the semidefinite inequalities to the limit.
proof_scope.321F: Proves the planar isoperimetric inequality and circle equality for C2 positive-curvature convex curves via the support-area formula, Stokes, and a Fejer/Fourier proof of Wirtinger's inequality. Does not claim a proof for arbitrary nonconvex curves.

remaining_branches: The report's main model and result branches are represented, but no full proof of polynomial/algebraic Birkhoff rigidity, central strip rigidity, outer-area rigidity, symplectic rigidity, or effective measure bounds is supplied. These are explicitly cited research theorems with their hypotheses.

Birkhoff's graph theorem, Aubry-Mather existence, beta strict convexity and differentiability, and the rational invariant-curve equivalence are cited inputs. Only rotation-number existence, the finite variational calculations, and the m-set Hessian/closedness argument are proved locally.

The beta comparison and equality theorems retain external proofs. The circular extremum, support-generator trial action and constant-width endpoint are computed locally. Irrational classical equality allows the Gutkin exception; outer-area comparison is not included in Theorem 6.7.

Magnetic/Minkowski rigidity and the general outer-length twist construction remain cited. Strong or variable magnetic fields, general outer-length integrability rigidity, partial-region outer-area rigidity, arbitrary two-value elliptic spectral recovery, and the boundary-local Birkhoff problem remain open as described in the report.

Wire examples and cone angular-momentum conservation are proved locally. Finite-reflection and orbit-separation theorems for cones, as well as the C2 counterexample, remain external. No independence or Poisson commutation is asserted for the separating integrals. Closed nonplanar three-dimensional wire examples and degenerate/nonconvex cone extensions remain open.
No report figures are reproduced and no image-specific claim is imported. Global deduplication, normalizeFormat, full Forester build and browser rendering belong to the parent integration task.
normalization_notes: Author metadata is author, date is 2026-10-19. Knowledge bodies use Forester inline/display math and direct mathematical exposition, with no manual related-pages blocks.
The generating-function convention is p=-S_1, P=S_2 and S_12<0 for positive twist. Positive length/area local maxima use the opposite action sign to Aubry-Mather minimization.

Beta is negative maximal inner length or inner area per vertex, and positive minimal outer length or outer area per vertex. BBS section 3.3 prose mentioning maximal circumscribed area is not used to reverse the minimizing-action convention.
For symplectic billiards, -det(x,y)/2 means negative triangle area, not negative half of the triangle area. This fixes the circular value -R^2*sin(2*pi*rho)/2.
Theorem 6.7 compares length models with a disc of the same perimeter and the symplectic model with a disc of the same area. It does not cover outer-area billiards.

The rational equality assertion is restricted to 0<rho<1/2. At rho=1/2, classical equality is constant width rather than circularity, symplectic beta vanishes for every table, and the outer actions diverge. This endpoint qualification follows the supplementary exact statement and a direct calculation.

A real order-k linear map is conjugate to R_(2*pi*m/k) for a primitive residue m, not necessarily to the particular generator R_(2*pi/k). Its cyclic subgroup is conjugate to the usual order-k rotation group; the finite-symmetry consequences use that subgroup fact.

Polynomial integrability requires a velocity-polynomial integral nonconstant on the unit-energy level. Glutsyuk's smooth bounded-domain corollary does not require the boundary to be algebraic a priori.

The m-set is defined by actual finite fixed-endpoint local maxima. Semidefinite finite Hessians and definite proper-subinterval Hessians are equivalent across all intervals because the mixed derivatives are positive. Closedness uses the semidefinite formulation, not closedness of negative definiteness alone.
The ellipse equation in 320A is x^2/a+y^2/b=1 with a>b>0, so a,b are squared semiaxes. The circular/outer-area ellipse families are homothetic; classical elliptic caustics are confocal.

The nonstandard support generator uses canonical p equal to negative signed distance with the stated right-normal convention. This fixes the first-derivative signs and yields negative perimeter as periodic action.
Global total integrability, phase-boundary local integrability, closeness of a table to an ellipse, polynomial integrability, and cone orbit separation are separate notions throughout.

The prerequisite registry below includes only actual body-linked mathematical prerequisites, not every consequence or comparison link. In particular, reciprocal exposition links between 320C and 320D are not registered as a prerequisite cycle.

source_errata: Main Corollary 3.3 omits an explicit atomless restriction in its compressed wording. The notes use the atomless ergodic setting supplied by Corollary 3.2 and do not claim that finite ergodic cycles are all weakly equivalent.
Main section 3.4's compressed Rokhlin=KS amenable phrase is restricted in the notes to free ergodic infinite amenable actions. Finite periodic actions show why the restriction matters.

Main Theorem 2.3's finite-generator discussion is used with the standard nonatomic setting from Seward's precise theorem, not as a prescribed-generator assertion for arbitrary finite probability spaces.
